cor-add-projection.title: Backfitting as alternating projection
cor-add-projection.html: If λj=0 for every j and each Zj has full column rank, then each Sj is the orthogonal projection onto Vj=C(Zj) by @thm-proj-sym-idem, and backfitting converges to the orthogonal projection of y onto V0+V1+⋯+Vq. The fitted components are unique iff the only way to write 0 as ∑jvj with vj∈Vj is with every vj=0.

def-add-concurvity-index.title: Concurvity
def-add-concurvity-index.html:
Let V0=C(X) and Vj=C(Zj) be the model spaces of the terms, all centred so that Vj⊆1⊥ for j≥1. The terms exhibit exact concurvity if there exist vj∈Vj, not all zero, with ∑j≥0vj=0. The concurvity index of term j is κj=max{‖M−jv‖2‖v‖2:v∈Vj, v≠0}∈[0,1],{#eq-add-concurvity}

where M−j is the orthogonal projection onto ∑k≠jVk. Equivalently κj is the largest squared canonical correlation between Vj and ∑k≠jVk, and κj=1 iff there is exact concurvity involving term j.

def-add-model.title: Additive model
def-add-model.html:
Let (yi,x(i),zi1,…,ziq), i=1,…,n, be observed, where x(i)⊤ is the ith row of an n×p matrix X whose first column is 1. The additive model is 𝛃yi=x(i)⊤β+∑j=1qfj(zij)+εi,E(εi)=0, Var(εi)=σ2,{#eq-add-model}

with the εi uncorrelated, the fj unknown smooth functions, and the identifiability constraints ∑i=1nfj(zij)=0,j=1,…,q.{#eq-add-centring}

The vector 𝛈𝛃η=Xβ+∑jfj, where fj={fj(z1j),…,fj(znj)}⊤, is the additive predictor. If X=1 the model is purely additive; otherwise it is a partial linear or semiparametric model.

def-add-spatial.title: Geoadditive model
def-add-spatial.html:
Let si be the location of observation i. The geoadditive model is the additive model @eq-add-model with one extra term, 𝛃yi=x(i)⊤β+∑j=1qfj(zij)+fgeo(si)+εi,∑ifgeo(si)=0.{#eq-add-geoadditive}

Two cases are distinguished by the kind of location.

  1. (Areal data.) si∈{1,…,D} names one of D regions. The design is the incidence matrix Zgeo with (Zgeo)is=1 if si=s and 0 otherwise, the coefficient γs is the effect of region s, and the penalty is built from a neighbourhood structure: a symmetric relation s∼t saying which regions share a border.

  2. (Point-referenced data.) si∈R2 is a coordinate pair. The design is (Zgeo)il=r(‖si−κl‖) for a set of knots κ1,…,κL and a radial function r, and the penalty is Pgeo={r(‖κl−κm‖)}lm.

def-add-star.title: Structured additive regression
def-add-star.html:
A structured additive predictor is 𝛈𝛃𝛄η=Xβ+∑j=1JZjγj,{#eq-add-star}

where X collects the unpenalized columns and each term j is a pair (Zj,Pj) with Zj an n×dj design block and Pj a symmetric nonnegative definite dj×dj penalty matrix, identified by the constraint 𝛄1⊤Zjγj=0 of @prp-add-identifiability(c). A structured additive regression model (STAR) fits @eq-add-star by minimizing the penalized criterion @eq-add-criterion, with one smoothing parameter λj≥0 per term.

def-add-varying.title: Varying-coefficient model
def-add-varying.html:
Let u1,…,un be the values of an interaction variable and z1,…,zn those of an effect modifier. A varying-coefficient term is f(zi)ui,∑i=1nf(zi)=0,{#eq-add-varying}

and the varying-coefficient model is a structured additive model (@def-add-model) in which one or more of the terms have this form. Combined with a parametric column u=(u1,…,un)⊤ carrying a coefficient βu, the total effect of u on the response is E(yi)=⋯+{βu+f(zi)}ui,{#eq-add-varying-slope}

so that βu+f(z) is the coefficient function: the slope in u at effect modifier value z. With ui≡1 the term is an ordinary smooth main effect, and with f constrained to be constant it is an ordinary linear effect.

exm-add-backfit.title: Backfitting on two P-spline terms
exm-add-backfit.html:
Two covariates on [0,1] come from a bivariate normal pair squashed through a hyperbolic tangent, so one correlation ρ controls their dependence; the mean is 3+f1(z1)+f2(z2), cubic-like in the first component and a bump in the second, with normal errors of standard deviation 0.4. With n=400, 15 cubic B-splines per term, second-difference penalties and λ1=λ2=8.0, backfitting and one direct solve of @eq-add-normal agree to 9.4×10−14 in the fitted values, as they must, using 11.64 effective degrees of freedom: 1 for the intercept, 5.34 and 5.30 for the two components.

The work is not shared. At ρ=0.0 the backfitting change falls below 10−12 after 9 cycles, shrinking by a factor of about 0.015 per cycle; at ρ=0.5 it takes 21 cycles and the factor is 0.240; at ρ=0.9 it takes 121 cycles and the factor is 0.674. Figure 44.2.1 shows the fitted components and the three convergence curves, straight on a logarithmic scale as @thm-add-backfitting(c) predicts.

exm-add-concurvity.title: Two covariates, one relation
exm-add-concurvity.html: Let z1 be uniform on [0,1] and z2=z11.5+noise, and fit two P-spline terms with λ=5.0 to n=300 observations. The design is fixed and the criterion quadratic, so @prp-add-df(c) gives the exact standard deviation of each component without simulation. As the noise falls from 0.30 through 0.10 to 0.03, the concurvity index of the first term climbs from 0.609 to 0.933 to 0.994, and the standard deviation of the first component at z1=0.3 climbs from 0.049 to 0.087 to 0.207, an inflation of 4.2; over the same range the standard deviation of the fitted mean there moves only from 0.094 to 0.080. The fit is fine; its attribution to the two covariates is not.

exm-add-constraint.title: Two P-spline blocks
exm-add-constraint.html: Take q=2, a cubic B-spline basis of 15 functions on equally spaced knots for each covariate, and the second-difference penalty of @def-smo-pspline. Unconstrained, each block has 15 columns summing to 1 row by row and a penalty of rank 13; after @prp-add-identifiability(c) it has 14 columns summing to zero and a penalty of the same rank, so Z=[1,Z1,Z2] has 29 columns. Of the two unpenalized directions per block, constant and linear trend, the constraint removes one: the term still fits a straight line in zj free of charge, but not an arbitrary level.

exm-add-gam.title: Physician visits, with two smooth terms
exm-add-gam.title_html: Physician visits, with two smooth terms
exm-add-gam.html:
@exm-cnt-visits fitted a Poisson log-linear model to the RAND Health Insurance Experiment, n=20190 person-years, with every regressor entering linearly — among them a general disease index, which has no reason to be linear on the log scale. Take that index and one further variable of the same kind, the log of the participation incentive payment, and give each a P-spline term of 12 basis functions, keeping the coinsurance, deductible-plan, physical-limitation and health-status regressors linear: that is a generalized additive model, fitted by @eq-add-pirls. Its baseline throughout is the linear fit, meaning the same list of regressors with the disease index and the incentive payment entering linearly too.

The disease term takes 9.11 effective degrees of freedom and the incentive term 4.48, out of 20.59 for the whole model. The estimated dispersion is 6.22, so these data are as overdispersed as Chapter 37 found them; the smoothing parameters, 1.16 and 103.94, were chosen with that dispersion in place. The coefficient of log coinsurance is −0.1146, a rate ratio of 0.8917, against −0.0874 in the linear fit and −0.0712 in the smaller model of @exm-cnt-visits, which carried no incentive-payment term at all; self-reported physical limitation still multiplies the rate by e0.2777.

The deviance falls from 84378 for the linear fit to 83619, at a cost of 11.59 degrees of freedom. Scaling by the dispersion gives a quasi-F statistic of 10.54 on 11.59 and 20169 degrees of freedom, whose nominal p-value is 1.6×10−20. The deviance difference is the statistic of @thm-glm-deviance(a), but its reference distribution there assumed a fixed nested pair, and here the larger model was smoothed. Read as a rough diagnostic rather than as a test, it says what panel (a) of Figure 44.6.1 shows: the effect of the disease index is far from linear — it rises steeply over the first half of the range and then flattens — and no straight line would do.

The same panel is a warning. Above a disease index of 40 lie 55 person-years, 0.3% of the sample, and the curve there swings by more than a unit on the log scale with a standard error of 0.347, against 0.011 at the median. That wiggle is an artefact of a handful of observations and a globally chosen smoothing parameter; report it as “no information above 40”, not as a finding.

exm-add-map.title: Smoothing a district map
exm-add-map.html:
A simulated country is a 12×12 lattice of 144 districts with between 1 and 8 observations each, 604 in all. The response has mean 2+0.7x+surface(s), with x an ordinary covariate and the surface a smooth function of the district centroid that the model does not know; the errors are normal with standard deviation 0.9.

Figure 44.4.1 compares three fits. Unpenalized district effects use 143.0 degrees of freedom and give the noisy map of panel (b), with root mean squared error 0.579 against the true surface. The neighbourhood penalty @eq-add-mrf, with λ from the restricted likelihood, uses 45.5 and brings that down to 0.170. A kriging term on 21 knots uses 17.7 and gives 0.228: smoother still, and slightly too smooth, because the true surface has features the coarse knot grid cannot represent. The coefficient of x comes out at 0.581 with a standard error of 0.042 — against a true 0.7, about 2.8 standard errors low on this draw — and the residual standard deviation at 0.953.

exm-add-mrf-small.title: Four regions in a row
exm-add-mrf-small.html: Let four districts lie in a row, 1∼2∼3∼4: P=(1−100−12−100−12−100−11), with 𝛄𝛄γ⊤Pγ=(γ1−γ2)2+(γ2−γ3)2+(γ3−γ4)2, rank 3 and null space span{1}. If district 4 is instead an island with no neighbours, its row and column vanish, the rank drops to 2 and the null space is spanned by (1,1,1,0)⊤ and (0,0,0,1)⊤: the island is not penalized at all and is estimated from its own data alone.

exm-add-star.title: Four kinds of term at once
exm-add-star.title_html: Four kinds of term at once
exm-add-star.html:
A simulated data set of 1200 observations has a binary covariate with a linear effect, a smooth effect of z1, a coefficient of u varying with z2, an areal effect on an 8×8 map of 64 districts and a random intercept for 40 clusters: four terms, 132 coefficients, smoothing parameters from @eq-add-reml-update.

The fit recovers the residual standard deviation as 0.713 (true 0.7) and the linear effect as 0.770 (true 0.8). The four terms take 7.86, 5.13, 42.92 and 36.48 effective degrees of freedom, 94.40 out of 132, with implied variance components 0.1609, 0.0170, 0.2002 and 0.2646 — the last the variance of the random intercept, truly 0.25. Root mean squared errors against the truth are 0.031, 0.045, 0.129 and 0.119, against a noise standard deviation of 0.7. Figure 44.5.1 shows all four.

exm-add-statecrime.title: Does poverty matter more in urban states?
exm-add-statecrime.title_html: Does poverty matter more in urban states?
exm-add-statecrime.html:
@exm-proj-fwl-crime fitted the murder rate of the 50 US states in 2009 on the poverty rate, the single-parent percentage and the urban percentage, reporting one coefficient for poverty. Here that coefficient may vary smoothly with how urban the state is: murderi=β0+β1singlei+{β2+f(urbani)}(povertyi−poverty―)+f0(urbani)+εi, with P-spline terms of 8 basis functions for f and f0 and smoothing parameters chosen by the restricted-likelihood updates of Section 44.5. The fit uses 6.83 effective degrees of freedom in all, of which 1.82 go to the smooth main effect of urbanization and 2.01 to the coefficient function.

The average poverty slope is 0.250. Keeping the smooth main effect of urbanization but forcing the poverty slope to be constant gives 0.231, and @exm-proj-fwl-crime, in which urbanization entered linearly as well, gave 0.2538. The estimated coefficient function rises from −0.034 at 20% urban to 0.364 at 60% and falls back to 0.152 at 90%: on its face, a story in which poverty is associated with homicide in middling states and not in the most rural ones.

That story does not survive its standard errors. The band of ±2 standard errors in Figure 44.3.1 contains the constant coefficient over the whole range, and the contrast between 60% and 20% urban is 0.398 with a standard error of 0.234, a ratio of 1.70. Fifty states and a residual standard deviation of 1.418 murders per 100,000 cannot resolve a coefficient function; they can only say that one is not needed.

exr-add-backfit-one.title: A1
exr-add-backfit-one.html: Run backfitting with q=1. How many cycles does it take, and why?

exr-add-backfit-population.title: C1
exr-add-backfit-population.html: Population backfitting. Let Z1,Z2 be random with E(Y2)<∞, and consider minimizing E{Y−g1(Z1)−g2(Z2)}2 over centred square-integrable g1,g2. Show that the minimizers satisfy g1(z)=E{Y−g2(Z2)∣Z1=z}−c and symmetrically, and that the sample algorithm of this section is the empirical version with conditional expectation replaced by a smoother.

exr-add-catalogue.title: A1
exr-add-catalogue.html: For each of the following, give the design block and the penalty: (i) a random slope of a covariate u within K clusters; (ii) a linear effect that is not to be penalized at all; (iii) a smooth term that is to be penalized towards a straight line rather than towards a constant.

exr-add-column-centring.title: B1
exr-add-column-centring.html: Let Zj be a B-spline block with the partition-of-unity property, so Zj1=1, and let Pj be a difference penalty, so Pj1=0. Show that centring the columns, that is replacing Zj by (I−n−111⊤)Zj, makes Zj⊤Zj+λjPj singular, while the reparameterization of @prp-add-identifiability(c) does not.

exr-add-concurvity-uncorrelated.title: B3
exr-add-concurvity-uncorrelated.html: Let z1 be uniform on [−1,1] and z2=z12. Show that Cov(z1,z2)=0, so the two covariates are uncorrelated, and yet the two model spaces of quadratic functions exhibit exact concurvity. What does this say about diagnosing concurvity by a correlation matrix?

exr-add-curse.title: A1
exr-add-curse.html: Repeat the neighbourhood calculation of Section 44.1: what side length does a cube-shaped neighbourhood need in order to contain 1% of n points uniformly spread over the unit cube in q dimensions, for q=1,3,10? At what q does the required side exceed 0.5?

exr-add-df-monotone.title: B2
exr-add-df-monotone.html: Show that dfj in @eq-add-edf is nonincreasing in λj. Hint: work with one term and no parametric part first, where df(λ)=∑kθk/(θk+λ) for the eigenvalues θk of Zj⊤Zj in the metric of Pj.

exr-add-gam-boundary-count.title: C1
exr-add-gam-boundary-count.html: In @exm-add-gam the curve above a disease index of 40 rests on 55 observations. Suppose all of them were deleted. Using the fact that the P-spline penalty of @def-smo-pspline has the straight lines as its null space, describe exactly what the fitted curve does over the empty range, and compute the limit of its variance as the range of emptiness grows.

exr-add-gam-phi.title: A1
exr-add-gam-phi.html: In @thm-add-gam(a) the dispersion cancels from the iteration but not from the smoothing-parameter update. Explain the difference, and say what happens to the fitted curves if ϕ=1 is assumed when in truth ϕ=6.

exr-add-gcv-vs-reml.title: B2
exr-add-gcv-vs-reml.html: Write the generalized cross-validation criterion @def-sel-gcv for a STAR fit as 𝛌GCV(λ)=n‖y−Sy‖2/(n−trS)2. Show that it is minimized where σ2 of @eq-add-reml-update is stationary in a particular sense, and explain why the two criteria nevertheless disagree in general.

exr-add-interaction.title: C1
exr-add-interaction.html: An additive model has no interactions. Show that if the true mean is f(z1,z2)=z1z2 on [0,1]2 with z1,z2 independent and uniform, the best additive approximation in mean square, argming1,g2E{(Z1Z2−g1(Z1)−g2(Z2))2} subject to Eg1(Z1)=Eg2(Z2)=0, is g1(z)=(z−12)/2, g2(z)=(z−12)/2 plus the constant 1/4, and compute the mean squared approximation error.

exr-add-island.title: A1
exr-add-island.html: A map has two islands, each a connected group of districts, with no neighbour pairs between them. What is rank(P), what does the penalty leave unidentified, and what does the centring constraint of @prp-add-identifiability(c) fix?

exr-add-local-scoring.title: B1
exr-add-local-scoring.html: Local scoring. Show that replacing the direct solve in @eq-add-pirls by one or more backfitting cycles on the weighted penalized normal equations gives the local scoring algorithm of Hastie and Tibshirani, and that @thm-add-backfitting applies to the inner loop with Zj⊤Zj replaced by Zj⊤WZj. What must be true of W for the convergence proof to go through?

exr-add-modified.title: B2
exr-add-modified.html: Modified backfitting. Suppose the smoothers Sj are not of the form @eq-add-blocksmoother but are symmetric with eigenvalues in [0,1] and satisfy Sj1=1. Show that replacing Sj by Sjc=(I−n−111⊤)Sj makes every fitted component sum to zero at each step, and that A in @thm-add-backfitting is then replaced by a matrix with the same structure acting on 1⊥.

exr-add-mrf-chain-equals-difference.title: B1
exr-add-mrf-chain-equals-difference.html: Show that on a chain 1∼2∼⋯∼D, the penalty @eq-add-mrf equals the first-difference penalty 𝛄𝛄γ⊤D1⊤D1γ of @def-smo-pspline, and that the second-difference penalty is not of the form @eq-add-mrf for any neighbourhood structure with nonnegative off-diagonal weights.

exr-add-mrf-conditional.title: B2
exr-add-mrf-conditional.html: Using @prp-add-mrf(c), show that if district s has ns neighbours and its own ms observations with mean y¯s, and all other effects are held fixed, the penalized criterion is minimized over γs at a weighted average of y¯s and the neighbour mean, with weights ms and λns. What happens when ms=0?

exr-add-partial-linear.title: B3
exr-add-partial-linear.html: In @def-add-model take q=1 and let X be a general parametric design. Show that the penalized estimate of 𝛃β is 𝛃β^={X⊤(I−S1)X}−1X⊤(I−S1)y where S1=Z1(Z1⊤Z1+λ1P1)−1Z1⊤ — the Frisch–Waugh–Lovell form of @thm-proj-fwl with the smoother in place of a projection. What changes in the proof?

exr-add-random-is-ridge.title: B1
exr-add-random-is-ridge.html: Take one term with Z=D the n×K matrix of cluster indicators and P=I. Show that the penalized estimate of the cluster effects is γ^k=mkr¯k/(mk+λ), where mk is the cluster size and r¯k the mean residual in cluster k, and identify this with @thm-mix-blup for the one-way random effects model of @def-mix-oneway.

exr-add-reml-not-monotone.title: C1
exr-add-reml-not-monotone.html: The updates @eq-add-reml-update are a fixed-point iteration, not a descent method, and they are not guaranteed to converge from every start. Construct a two-term model in which the restricted likelihood has a stationary point at τ12=0 (the term is smoothed away), verify that this is a fixed point of @eq-add-reml-update, and explain how a run that lands there should be reported.

exr-add-select.title: B2
exr-add-select.html: Shrinking a whole term away. Let Pj have null space of dimension mj with orthonormal basis Pj0, and replace the penalty by Pj+ϵPj0Pj0⊤ for a small ϵ>0. Show that the new penalty is positive definite, that λj→∞ now shrinks the whole term to zero, and that dfj→0.

exr-add-spatial-confounding.title: C1
exr-add-spatial-confounding.html: Let v be the vector of a covariate that is constant within each district, so that v∈C(Zgeo) for the incidence design. Show that in the unpenalized geoadditive model the coefficient of v is not identified at all, and that with a penalty it is identified but its estimate depends on λgeo, tending to the no-spatial-term estimate as λgeo→∞. What does this say about reporting such a coefficient?

exr-add-tensor.title: C1
exr-add-tensor.html: Build the smallest tensor-product term by hand: take d1=d2=3 basis functions in each coordinate and first-difference penalties P(1)=P(2). Write out the 9×9 penalty of @eq-add-tensor for λ1=λ2=1 and find its null space. Why does that null space make the term identifiable only after the main effects have been constrained away?

exr-add-time-varying.title: B1
exr-add-time-varying.html: A varying-coefficient model is fitted to a time series, but the errors follow 𝛆Cov(ε)=σ2V with V≠I. Show that the penalized estimate 𝛄γ^=A−1Z⊤y is still unbiased for the penalized target A−1Z⊤E(Y), but that its covariance is σ2A−1Z⊤VZA−1, not σ2A−1Z⊤ZA−1. If V has positive autocorrelations, in which direction is the naive band wrong?

exr-add-two-block-rate.title: B1
exr-add-two-block-rate.html: For q=2 with no parametric part, show that the Gauss–Seidel iteration matrix T of @eq-add-gauss-seidel has spectral radius equal to the largest eigenvalue of A11−1A12A22−1A21, and that for unpenalized one-column blocks this is the squared correlation between the two columns.

exr-add-varying-concurvity.title: B2
exr-add-varying-concurvity.html: Show that a model containing both a smooth main effect f0(z) and a varying-coefficient term f(z)u has exact concurvity (@def-add-concurvity-index) as soon as ui is itself a function of zi, say ui=h(zi) with h in the span of the basis. What does this say about the model of @exm-add-statecrime?

exr-add-varying-special.title: A1
exr-add-varying-special.html: What does a varying-coefficient term become when (i) ui≡1; (ii) f is forced to be constant; (iii) f is forced to be linear in z? Which of the three has a familiar name from Part II?

prp-add-concurvity.title: What concurvity does
prp-add-concurvity.html:
With the notation of @def-add-concurvity-index and λj=0 for all j:

  1. A=Z⊤Z is singular iff there is exact concurvity. The fitted values are unaffected — they are the projection onto ∑jVj — but the decomposition into components is not unique.

  2. Assume in addition that there is no exact concurvity and that each Zj has full column rank. Then there is a direction v∈Vj, v≠0, with Var(v⊤f^j)=σ2‖v‖21−κj,{#eq-add-variance-inflation}

    against the value σ2‖v‖2 that the same functional would have if Vj were orthogonal to the other spaces. The inflation factor is 1/(1−κj), and in the single-column case Vj=span{xj} it is the variance inflation factor of @def-col-vif, with Var(β^j)=σ2/{‖xj‖2(1−κj)}.

  3. (What a penalty repairs.) With λj>0 for every j and N(Zj)∩N(Pj)={0}, the matrix A is nonsingular and the fitted components are unique, whatever κj may be.

prp-add-df.title: Smoother matrix and degrees of freedom
prp-add-df.title_html: Smoother matrix and degrees of freedom
prp-add-df.html:
Suppose A=Z⊤Z+P is nonsingular, and let C=A−1Z⊤, so that 𝛄γ^=Cy. Write Cj=ZjC[j], where C[j] holds the rows of C belonging to the jth block.

  1. The fitted vector is y^=Sy with S=ZA−1Z⊤, a symmetric matrix whose eigenvalues lie in [0,1]; the fitted jth component is f^j=Cjy, and S=XC[0]+∑jCj.

  2. The effective degrees of freedom of the fit and of its terms are df=trS=tr(A−1Z⊤Z),dfj=trCj=dj−λjtr{(A−1)jjPj},{#eq-add-edf}

    and they add: df=p+∑jdfj. Each dfj decreases from dj at λj=0 towards dim⁡N(Pj) as λj→∞.

  3. If Cov(Y)=σ2I, then 𝛄Cov(γ^)=σ2A−1Z⊤ZA−1 and Cov(f^j)=σ2CjCj⊤.

prp-add-identifiability.title: Identifiability of the components
prp-add-identifiability.html:
Write Vj for the linear space of vectors {g(z1j),…,g(znj)}⊤ as g ranges over the functions the jth term is allowed to take, and assume 1∈Vj for each j.

  1. If 𝛃(β,f1,…,fq) and 𝛃(β~,f~1,…,f~q) give the same additive predictor and both satisfy @eq-add-centring, then every difference fj−f~j is orthogonal to 1, and so is 𝛃𝛃X(β−β~)=−∑j(fj−f~j). If in addition the centred spaces C(X)∩1⊥, V1∩1⊥,…,Vq∩1⊥ admit no nontrivial relation — no exact concurvity, the condition studied in Section 44.2 — then 𝛃𝛃Xβ=Xβ~ and fj=f~j for every j.

  2. Without @eq-add-centring the components are determined only up to constants that sum to zero: replacing fj by fj+cj with ∑jcj=0 leaves 𝛈η unchanged.

  3. If 𝛄fj=Zjγj for a design block Zj, the constraint 𝛄1⊤Zjγj=0 is imposed exactly by writing 𝛄𝛂γj=Ujαj, where the columns of Uj are an orthonormal basis of 𝛄𝛄{γ:1⊤Zjγ=0}: minimizing any criterion over 𝛂αj with design ZjUj and penalty Uj⊤PjUj is the same as minimizing it over 𝛄γj subject to the constraint.

prp-add-kriging.title: Low-rank kriging is a penalized term
prp-add-kriging.title_html: Low-rank kriging is a penalized term
prp-add-kriging.html:
Let R={r(‖κl−κm‖)}lm be the correlation matrix of the field at L knots, assumed positive definite, and let u={U(κ1),…,U(κL)}⊤∼NL(0,τ2R).

  1. The best linear predictor of U(s) from u is U^(s)=r(s)⊤R−1u with r(s)={r(‖s−κ1‖),…,r(‖s−κL‖)}⊤. Writing 𝛄γ=R−1u, the fitted spatial effect at the observations is 𝛄Zgeoγ with (Zgeo)il=r(‖si−κl‖), and 𝛄γ∼NL(0,τ2R−1).

  2. Consequently the log-density of 𝛄γ contributes 𝛄𝛄γ⊤Rγ/(2τ2), so the penalized criterion @eq-add-criterion with Pgeo=R and λgeo=σ2/τ2 has as its minimizer the posterior mode of 𝛄γ — the kriging predictor restricted to the span of the L knots.

  3. Taking every distinct location as a knot recovers exact kriging, that is, generalized least squares with the covariance τ2R+σ2I of Chapter 31; taking L≪n knots is the low-rank approximation that makes the term cheap.

prp-add-mixed.title: A STAR model is a linear mixed model
prp-add-mixed.title_html: A STAR model is a linear mixed model
prp-add-mixed.html:
Let Pj have rank rj and spectral decomposition Pj=Pj+ΛjPj+⊤ with Λj=diag(νj1,…,νjrj) positive, and let Pj0 be an orthonormal basis of N(Pj). Put 𝛄Xj0=ZjPj0,Zj+=ZjPj+Λj−1/2,uj=Λj1/2Pj+⊤γj.{#eq-add-mixed-transform}

  1. 𝛄Zjγj=Xj0bj+Zj+uj with 𝛄bj=Pj0⊤γj, and 𝛄𝛄γj⊤Pjγj=‖uj‖2.

  2. With τj2=σ2/λj, the penalized criterion @eq-add-criterion divided by σ2 is the criterion @eq-mix-penalized of @thm-mix-henderson for the linear mixed model @eq-mix-model with fixed design [X,X10,…,XJ0], random design [Z1+,…,ZJ+], G=diag(τ12Ir1,…,τJ2IrJ) and R=σ2I.

  3. Consequently the penalized estimate is the BLUP of @thm-mix-blup; the smoothing parameters are variance ratios, λj=σ2/τj2; and the restricted likelihood @eq-mix-reml-loglik of the transformed model is a likelihood for (σ2,τ12,…,τJ2), hence for (λ1,…,λJ).

prp-add-mrf.title: The neighbourhood penalty
prp-add-mrf.html:
Let the regions 1,…,D carry a symmetric neighbourhood relation with no region its own neighbour, and let P be as in @eq-add-mrf.

  1. P is symmetric and nonnegative definite, and 𝛄𝛄γ⊤Pγ=∑s∼t(γs−γt)2.

  2. N(P) is spanned by the indicator vectors of the connected components of the neighbourhood graph. In particular rank(P)=D−c where c is the number of components, and N(P)=span{1} iff the graph is connected.

  3. Treating 𝛄𝛄exp⁡{−γ⊤Pγ/(2τ2)} as a density in 𝛄γ on N(P)⊥, the conditional distribution of γs given the others, for a region with ns≥1, is normal with mean ns−1∑t∼sγt, the average of its neighbours, and variance τ2/ns. The prior is therefore a Gaussian Markov random field: each region is shrunk towards its neighbours, and a region with many neighbours is shrunk harder. A region with ns=0 contributes nothing to the quadratic form: its coefficient is unpenalized, its conditional is flat, and it is estimated from its own data alone (@exm-add-mrf-small, @exr-add-island).

prp-add-reml-update.title: Restricted-likelihood updates
prp-add-reml-update.html:
In the mixed-model representation of @prp-add-mixed, the expectation-maximization algorithm for the variance components, with (b,u) as the missing data, updates 𝛄𝛄τj2,new=1rj[γ^j⊤Pjγ^j+σ2tr{(A−1)jjPj}],{#eq-add-em-update}

where 𝛄γ^j and A are computed at the current 𝛌λ. A pair 𝛕(τ2,σ2) is a fixed point of @eq-add-em-update together with the update σ2,new=‖y−y^‖2/(n−df) if and only if 𝛄𝛄τ^j2=γ^j⊤Pjγ^jdfj−mj,σ^2=‖y−y^‖2n−df,λ^j=σ^2τ^j2,{#eq-add-reml-update}

with mj=dj−rj=dim⁡N(Pj) and dfj, df the effective degrees of freedom of @prp-add-df.

prp-add-star-identified.title: When a STAR model is identified
prp-add-star-identified.title_html: When a STAR model is identified
prp-add-star-identified.html: In @def-add-star, assume every Zj has full column rank. The penalized criterion has a unique minimizer for every λj>0 if and only if the only vector 𝛄𝛃𝛄γ=(β⊤,γ1⊤,…)⊤ with 𝛃𝛄Xβ+∑jZjγj=0 and 𝛄Pjγj=0 for every j is 𝛄γ=0. Equivalently: there is no exact concurvity among C(X) and the unpenalized parts ZjN(Pj) of the terms.

prp-add-varying-fit.title: A varying-coefficient term is an ordinary penalized term
prp-add-varying-fit.title_html: A varying-coefficient term is an ordinary penalized term
prp-add-varying-fit.html:
Let B1,…,Bd be a basis for the effect modifier and P0 the penalty that the corresponding smooth main effect would use. Put (Z)il=uiBl(zi).

  1. With f=∑lγlBl, the vector of the term’s contributions is 𝛄{f(zi)ui}i=Zγ, and the roughness of f is 𝛄𝛄γ⊤P0γ as before. The term is therefore the pair (Z,P0), and everything in Sections 44.1 and 44.2 applies unchanged.

  2. The constraint @eq-add-varying is 𝛄c⊤γ=0 with c=(∑iB1(zi),…,∑iBd(zi))⊤ — the unweighted column sums of the basis, not of Z — and is absorbed by @prp-add-identifiability(c). Under it, βu in @eq-add-varying-slope is the average of the coefficient function over the design points, βu=n−1∑i{βu+f(zi)}.

  3. If ui≠0 for at least d design points with distinct zi and the basis is linearly independent there, Z has full column rank. Observations with ui=0 contribute nothing to the term: the coefficient function is estimated only where the interaction variable is nonzero.

thm-add-backfitting.title: Backfitting
thm-add-backfitting.html:
Consider the criterion @eq-add-criterion with blocks Z0=X, P0=0 and Z1,…,Zq, and write Ajj=Zj⊤Zj+λjPj, assumed nonsingular for every j. Let A=Z⊤Z+P as in @eq-add-normal, so that A is nonnegative definite with diagonal blocks Ajj.

  1. (Coordinate descent.) The backfitting update of the jth block is the exact minimizer of Q over 𝛄γj with all other blocks held fixed. In particular Q never increases along the iteration.

  2. (Gauss–Seidel.) In terms of coefficients, the update is 𝛄𝛄γj←Ajj−1Zj⊤(y−∑k≠jZkγk), which is one block Gauss–Seidel sweep for the linear system 𝛄Aγ=Z⊤y. Fix any order of the blocks — the algorithm above takes them in the order 1,…,q,0 — and write A=L+D+L⊤ with D the block diagonal and L the strictly block lower triangular part in that order. One full cycle sends 𝛄γ to 𝛄Tγ+(D+L)−1Z⊤y with T=I−(D+L)−1A.{#eq-add-gauss-seidel}

  3. (Convergence.) Let 𝛄γ(t) be the iterates from any starting point and let 𝛄γ^ be any solution of 𝛄Aγ=Z⊤y. Then 𝛄𝛄A1/2(γ(t)−γ^)→0 geometrically. Consequently the fitted vector 𝛄Zγ(t) converges to 𝛄Zγ^, the criterion 𝛄Q(γ(t)) converges to its minimum, and 𝛄γ(t) itself converges to a minimizer of Q, which may depend on the starting point.

  4. (Uniqueness.) If A is positive definite, the limit is the unique solution A−1Z⊤y of @eq-add-normal, and the convergence is geometric in every norm.

thm-add-gam.title: Generalized additive models
thm-add-gam.html:
Let y1,…,yn be independent from an exponential dispersion family in the sense of @def-glm-model, with dispersion ϕ, variance function V, link g and mean μi=g−1(ηi), and let 𝛈𝛄η=Zγ be the structured additive predictor @eq-add-star with block penalty P as in @eq-add-blockpenalty. Define the penalized deviance 𝛄𝛄𝛄𝛄Q(γ)=D(γ)+γ⊤Pγ,{#eq-add-penlik}

with D the deviance of @def-glm-deviance, and let 𝛄γ^ minimize it.

  1. Minimizing @eq-add-penlik is the same as maximizing the penalized log-likelihood 𝛄𝛄𝛄ℓ(γ)−(2ϕ)−1γ⊤Pγ. Neither the minimizer nor the iteration below depends on ϕ.

  2. (Penalized IRLS.) With W the working weights and z the working response of @eq-glm-working-response, both evaluated at 𝛄γ(t), the Fisher scoring step for @eq-add-penlik is 𝛄γ(t+1)=(Z⊤WZ+P)−1Z⊤Wz,{#eq-add-pirls}

    that is, the penalized weighted least squares fit of the working response on the same design. At a fixed point the unpenalized columns satisfy 𝛍X⊤WD−1(y−μ)=0, where D=diag{h′(ηi)}; for the canonical link with prior weights wi≡1 this is 𝛍X⊤(y−μ)=0.

  3. (Degrees of freedom.) At convergence, with A=Z⊤WZ+P, the effective degrees of freedom are df=tr(A−1Z⊤WZ) and split over terms exactly as in @prp-add-df(b). The approximate covariance of 𝛄γ^ is ϕA−1Z⊤WZA−1 in its frequentist form and ϕA−1 in the Bayesian form of @prp-add-mixed.

  4. (Inference for a term.) Let Vj=ϕ(A−1)jj and let Vjr− be the rank-r pseudo-inverse of Vj with r the integer nearest to dfj. Under fj≡0, and treating 𝛌λ as fixed and ϕ as known, 𝛄𝛄Tj=γ^j⊤Vjr−γ^j has approximately the χ2(r) distribution; with ϕ estimated, Tj/r is referred to F(r,n−df). This is an approximation, stated here without proof; see the notes.
